utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So, good afternoon. Madam Registrar, could you call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes. Good afternoon, Your Honours. This is case number IT-03-68-T, the Prosecutor versus Naser Oric.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Oric, can you follow the proceedings in your own language?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honours, gentlemen. Yes, I can follow the proceedings in my mother tongue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Appearances for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours; and also good afternoon to the Defence. My name is Jan Wubben, lead counsel for the Prosecution. Together with me, Mr. Gramsci Di Fazio, Ms. Joanne Richardson, and our case manager, Ms. Donnica Henry-Frijlink.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Wubben, and good afternoon to you and your team. Appearances for Naser Oric.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honours. I am Vasvija Vidovic, and together with Mr. John Jones we represent Mr. Naser Oric. And we have our legal assistant, Ms. Adisa Mehic, and our CaseMap manager, Mr. Geoff Roberts, with us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Ms. Vidovic, and good afternoon to you and your team. Any preliminaries on your part? Of course, we will be dealing first and foremost with the Rule 68 matter concluded, and then tomorrow morning three Judges will meet and we'll decide what to do with it. So -- but if there is anything else you'd like to raise here now before we move to the Rule 68 business. I see none. So in the meantime, after the sitting on Thursday, Mr. Di Fazio provided the -- his submissions in writing, which I suppose you got too. Do you wish to respond or do you wish to leave everything as it is now and then leave the matter in our hands?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, just a very brief comment, since we do have an objection to the authenticity of the document. I will very briefly address that issue. I will very briefly talk about the motion by the Prosecution, if you allow me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Go ahead, by all means.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I will not be dealing any more with the fact whether this article is part of the subject material under Rule 68, but I'm concerned about the manner in which the Prosecution is interpreting Rule 68, and in general the application of Rule 68 and their adherence to Rule 68 in this case. After our discussion on the 17th of October, 2005, the Prosecutor provided us with materials for which he said were referring to the reaction of the Serb public to Nisic's interview in Vranjska Novine. Some of those reactions obviously contain very important material for the Defence which is again subject to Rule 68. Your Honours, I would now like the usher to distribute just one of the items among the material that was given to us, and it refers to the statement of Dejan Jevtic, commander of the special forces, special units of the Red Berets, and it's in regard to Nisic's interview. Unfortunately, the Prosecution gave us only a small part of the article. I would be interested in seeing the entire article, but even this small part of the article is very clear, and I'm going to quote from it. It's Dejan Jevtic is speaking, the commander of the special forces of the Red Berets.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters don't have the article in front of them.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He says: "Belgrade, Slobodan Nisic --"

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment, because I would like to make -- I am -- Usher -- okay. We are going to have copies distributed, or it's put on the ELMO. Right. Do you think you can work in all languages by that? Okay. All right. So let's -- I'm sorry for having interrupted you, Ms. Vidovic, but --

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No problem, Your Honours. I'm only going to read a very small part, the first part of this article. It states: "Top was not in, probably the Red Berets, Belgrade. Slobodan Misic Top was not or nor could he have been a member of the Red Berets, a special unit that I formed with some other people and which I commanded, Dejan Jevtic, commander of most of the actions of that unit conducted during the war on the Drina front told DT." So from this part you can see that the units of the Red Berets under the command of Dejan Jevtic were present on the Drina front throughout the war, which we have been proving and which all of the Prosecutor's witnesses that we questioned about the Red Berets denied. It's up you, Your Honours, to decide to which extent the Prosecution is violating Rule 68 and what their position is in regard to that obligation. And we have already been harmed a lot by being deprived of this material. What I would like to add is that I would like to have the Prosecution provide us with the complete article from this newspaper. It's an article from the 16th of November, 1997, and it was published in the Dnevni Telegraf newspaper. I would now like to talk very briefly about something else. I would like to respond to items 4, 5, and 6 of the Prosecutor's response regarding document P586, the alleged minutes of the -- or record of the District Court of Vranje. I would like to place this document P586 on the ELMO so that we could all see it again. I note, Your Honours, that we did not receive the translation of this document into English, but we were given the same version of the previous document, P585, to go with this document. We did not get an English translation for this document. I don't know whether the others have received the document. Could you please place the Bosnian version on the ELMO. Your Honours, this document we do not think is authentic. Namely, this document should be the record of the investigative activities of the District Court in Vranje. The area of the former Yugoslavia and the present-day Yugoslavia does not have the practice of tape recording court proceedings, and that is why the procedure of compiling or drafting all court documents, in particular records, is very formal and these records are drafted in a specific form. Your Honours, I would like to draw your attention -- could you please move the document up. Could you please return -- put it a little bit more down. Thank you. Each record should have the marking of the relevant court. So this should be the District Court Vranje. It should have the date and the number of the investigative action. We have it on the second page. However, from this record you can see that the accused were present as well as his Defence counsel, Dragan Nikolic. Could you please move the document up now. Your Honours, this record, as part of the investigative activities, should have been signed by all those present. Could you please move the page further up. Next to the stamp, on the right you can see that it states here "The accused," and you can see that there is no signature there. What is written here in this record would -- is allegedly a statement by the accused, and it should have been signed. This statement should also have been signed by his Defence counsel. What you actually have here is a signature by the name of the record-taker, and then beneath the words which state, "Investigative Judge," you have the words in Serbian "odiradni" [phoen] "certified" and you have something that should state "Misic," and then you have the stamp over that. You would not have in any similar procedure in the former Yugoslavia a stamp placed over the signature of the accused, as you have here. The accused should very clearly sign something as his own statement. Therefore, this is not something that would be a record of an investigation, and that is why we do not accept this document as authentic. Besides what we said on the previous occasion, it's evident from the statement which you received as document P585, that the accused in this case at this stage maintained his right to remain silent. Therefore, we do not accept this document as authentic. I would just very briefly also like to say something about item 12 of the Prosecutor's response. The Prosecutor states in that item that it is their right to decide who they will sue, and the Defence of course understands that the Prosecutor cannot indict all those who committed war crimes in the area of the former Yugoslavia and that the Prosecutor should focus on highly ranking figures. We searched all the available archives and all the cases conducted by the Prosecutor relating to the events in Podrinje in 1992, and determined that what is specific -- that Miroslav Deronjic specifically was indicted for the events in Glogova and sentenced to ten years, and we saw these documents ourselves. We also obtained documents relating to the camp in the area of Vlasenica. I simply do not believe that the Prosecutor simply failed to take into account facts which must have been known to him, these 70 to 80 killings in Podrinje in 1992, which they obviously knew and heard about. And I cannot believe that the Prosecutor failed to take into account other killings in Podrinje in 1992 which they knew about from different sources, that they simply tabled that, placed it in a drawer. And that is why I believe that the Prosecutor must have some other similar material in their possession, and with due respect, I would like to have the results of all the investigations relating to the killings of Muslims in Podrinje in 1992, or I would like then to be told that they do not have anything relating to the killings of Muslims in Podrinje in 1992. However, I cannot expect that. In this case, I see that the Prosecutor diligently processed the burning of houses in Fakovici, and I also accept that the Prosecutor processed the killings of such a number of people in this area, and this is the reason why we're requesting such material. Regarding the other matters from the response by the Prosecution, we leave that up to you to decide about, because we believe that we talked about that sufficiently on the 17th of October, 2005.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Di Fazio, do you want to respond to that? MR. DI FAZIO: If I could just be given a minute and a half to two minutes. Thanks.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, go ahead. MR. DI FAZIO: Thanks. Firstly with the newspaper article, with respect, the Defence has misunderstood. This is a Rule 68 issue that we're dealing with here. We do not conduct investigations on behalf of the Defence. We trawl our material to see what is Rule 68 and 66(B). If it fits that description, we hand it over. And that is the point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One -- let me stop you on this for a minute, because basically I think it all boils down to the following: Ms. Vidovic, if I read her well, wants the entire article. Is the entire article in your possession? This is the whole -- MR. DI FAZIO: That's exactly my point. That's exactly my point, if Your Honours please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: If you don't have it, then obviously I cannot ask you to go get it. MR. DI FAZIO: As presently advised, I understand that we do not have it. And that's the point. If we've got it, we'll look at it and make the decision in accordance with the Rules, and then hand it over. That's the point. Now, it may be that there's more to it outside in the wider world and in -- out there in the ether, so to speak. That's their job, the Defence's job. They must go and look for that material if they want to. If it's in our possession, we will divulge it in accordance with the Rules. That's the point I wanted to make. That point is also related to the latter point that was being made by Madam Vidovic and the impact of Exhibits 586 -- impact of Exhibit P586 on this issue. And she said the words, I think, that really go a long way to explaining some of the problems that we might have had, and she said this: "I simply do not believe --" Now -- "... that the Prosecution doesn't have more documents on this Misic business." In my submissions I took pains to point out to you that we conducted that very search. That issue was raised fairly and squarely by the Defence, and we addressed it fairly and squarely. Last week the Defence articulated the fear that they have. They said, and I don't say not sensibly, but they said there must have been more. There must be more material. We don't believe there isn't more material. This would have caused an investigation, would have generated more Rule 68 material. It was precisely that matter that the Defence went to -- sorry, that the Prosecution went to examine its records and see if they -- if indeed there were -- there was any other material that had been generated by the -- the issue of this man Misic suddenly arising in the newspapers in the way that it did, in order to see if there is any further disclosable material. Now, that has -- that exercise has been conducted. As I said, we generated an ISU search and we searched the material, as you may suspect, you know, with a fine-toothed comb. And the point that I seek to make is that it's -- one gets the impression that it's never going to be enough. We understand the concern that the Defence had about Slobodan Misic and we conducted an extremely thorough search into that man and into any possible documents that might have come into our possession as a result of OTP investigations. That's been done. The search has been collated, it's been searched through, and any disclosable material has now been handed over, and that's how the article in Cyrillic came to be -- came to be generated. So I -- I understand to a certain extent the Defence concerns, but I also want to allay them, if I may, by saying that the Prosecution takes very, very seriously its -- its Rule 68 obligations, and just because the Defence thinks there should be more documentation doesn't mean that there is. We've conducted our searches, gone through it, and handed over anything that could have been generated as a result of Misic. As far as the other issue of Rule -- P585 not being an authentic document, that is, in the Prosecution's submission, not something that's going to be able to assist you to decide this Rule 68 issue. Even if the document was not entirely correct according to knowledge that Madam Vidovic has, it could still use it to negate what is said in that newspaper article, and the whole point of it was the potency of the newspaper article. How much use could the Defence make of it? Everything that's been raised by Madam Vidovic today doesn't detract substantially from that particular submission. It's the use. What could they have done with it? What have they missed out on by this breach of Rule 68? And the Prosecution's submission is clear: Not much, by virtue of the operation of P585 and P586. And furthermore, if you look at P584, I don't think there's any suggestion that that's not authentic. That refers to decision number 59 of 97 in the first two lines, which is P586. It's decision number 59 of 97. Those are the matters that I wanted to put to you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. So basically what's going to happen now is tomorrow morning we will start discussing this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The concern -- please let me make one thing clear on behalf of everyone here, that the concerns of the Trial Chamber in matters related to the full application of Rule 68 should be the concerns of you all, Prosecution and Defence. For various reasons, obviously, but as far as we are concerned, it's because this is a matter of rights pertaining to the accused and obligations on the Prosecution arising out of -- out of the Rules, and there has to be strict observance of this Rule to its -- to the maximum, to the maximum number. So we will be dealing with that. On the other hand, before I close this chapter for the time being, and then we'll come down with our decision, I just wanted to know one thing from the Defence. In your motion you ask for sanctions. In your motions you ask for sanctions. What did you have in mind, Mr. Jones? I'm asking Mr. Jones or Madam Vidovic or whoever wishes to take the floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, I didn't -- Rule 68 bis obviously deals with failure to comply with disclosure obligations and refers to sanctions. I didn't specify because obviously it's a matter for the discretion of the Trial Chamber. Nonetheless, I -- one thing certainly which I think is important and which emerged during the course of the hearings last week is my submission certainly that the Prosecution didn't understand what was exculpatory because they didn't seem to understand that material which indicated that Red Berets or paramilitary units or volunteers from Serbia were present in Fakovici, or let's extend it to Kravica, Jezestica, Bjelovac, that they wouldn't consider that's exculpatory. And as much as Mr. Di Fazio has since made an admission that this was a Rule 68 breach, I was just trying to find the part in the transcript where his initial submission was there had been no breach in respect of one of the matters. So my concern is that if this matter then Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. is dealt with in one way or the other and I wouldn't say swept under the carpet, but if we move on beyond this, that more material would emerge subsequently which shows that there were volunteers in Kravica or volunteers in Bjelovac, and the Prosecution will say it's not exculpatory. So one idea I had in mind was that the Chamber might direct - maybe it's not a question of sanctions, but make clear to the Prosecution categories of material which obviously are exculpatory, and in that sense that would be something which would at least clarify what is and what is not exculpatory. We say there are a vast number of matters which impeach the credibility of Prosecution witnesses, whole hosts of issues which are exculpatory; anything showing that these villages posed a mortal threat to surrounding Muslim villages, for one, and that we don't want that to remain unclear because that will lead to further misunderstandings. So if that's not a sanction, it's at least a constructive way forward, in my submission.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Jones. Do you wish to comment on this, Mr. Di Fazio, or not? MR. DI FAZIO: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. So we adjourn on this matter. Of course we'll follow up with a written decision, which should be decided upon tomorrow, and then of course I have to sit down and draft the substantive part of it. So we expect it any time in the course of this week. All right? So no further preliminary matters? I see none. Usher, perhaps you could bring in this witness. Who is going to lead? Is it you, Madam Vidovic?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And how much time do you think you require?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, five or six hours at least. We have a lot of exhibits. Your Honours, just one brief -- just one brief remark. When the Prosecutor shows the witness exhibits, like they did the last time about the census, would they kindly show the witness the original in Bosnian and not like the last time when we had these documents in English, because this can cause quite significant misunderstandings, both for the Trial Chamber and for the witness. For example, I'm talking about Exhibit P587. And last time the witness was shown an excerpt in English. Not only a name can change, because it is important whether we're talking about Josevo or Joseva, or if there is no punctuation for first and last name. For example, the Prosecutor claimed a certain person was called Hasan but actually in the original it turned out that it was a woman named Hasan. So in order to prevent such misunderstandings which can confuse the witness, would the Prosecutor please always show the witness a document in the original Bosnian if the document is originally in Bosnian.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, and I suppose you take note of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. The other thing before we start with the witness, today we have got the consensus of everyone to have one break and finish at 6.15 instead of 7.00. All right? If that is all right with you, Madam Vidovic. Okay. Yes, let's bring the witness in. So it's six hours maximum on -- six hours for the Prosecution. How many hours with the Defence here and now? I mean subject, of course, as we go along you will be able to make a reassessment. Mr. Di Fazio. MR. DI FAZIO: I don't think it will be a quick one, if Your Honours please. As Madam Vidovic has rightly pointed out, there's numbers of documents to be shown, and I've got a few, and I suspect that I'll be using all of my time for cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. So this gentleman will be here with us I suppose practically to the end of the week.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good afternoon, to you, Mr. Ademovic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And I am the Presiding Judge, and I would like to welcome you on behalf of my two colleagues, Judge Brydensholt from the Kingdom of Denmark, Judge Eser from Germany, and myself. My name is Judge Agius, and I come from Malta. I welcome you to this Tribunal. You are a witness for the Defence and very soon you will start giving evidence. I will give you some further explanation when we are finished with this preliminary part. What I want to make sure first and foremost is what I'm saying in English is being interpreted to you in your own language and that you are receiving the interpretation in an adequate manner.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. It's all clear, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: If at any time there are problems with interpretation, either the level or you are not receiving it at all or the sound level is not to your satisfaction, please do let us know straight away and we will see into it. Before you start giving evidence, our Rules require that you make a solemn declaration equivalent to an oath. It's being handed to you now. Please read it out loud and that will be your solemn undertaking with us that you will be testifying the truth. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Mr. Ademovic. Please make yourself comfortable and I'll explain a few remaining things. Since you are a witness for the Defence, in other words, you've been summonsed to come over and give evidence by the Defence of Mr. Oric, it will be Madam Vidovic who is lead counsel for the accused in this trial who will examine you first. By examining you, I mean she will be asking you a number of questions which you are required to answer unless we tell you not to. Please try to cooperate as much as you can with Madam Vidovic and with the Trial Chamber by restricting your answers to the questions that are put to you. Don't try to give more information than you are being asked to give. And if a question can be answered by a mere yes or no, then answer it by a yes or a no. Otherwise, you are going to be here for a long time. Already assuming that you cooperate to the -- to the maximum, to the full, it will take Madam Vidovic at least today and tomorrow to finish with her examination-in-chief, and probably we would be even talking of Thursday. If we are talking of Thursday, there is a slight chance that you will need to remain here over the weekend if we don't finish with you. So the more you keep your answers short and to the point, the better chance you have of returning back home after Friday, or as soon as we finish with your testimony on Friday. Do you understand me?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour, I understand you. I understand completely. I would like to use this opportunity to greet all present, and I hope that my testimony will be of use for all of us. Thank you very much. We may begin.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you so much, Mr. Ademovic. And I think Madam Vidovic can start. Yes, Madam Vidovic. The break will be at 3.45 -- at 4.00. Sorry, at 4.00? At 4.00. Examined by Ms. Vidovic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Ademovic.

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon to you. Good afternoon to all present.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please tell the Trial Chamber your full first and last name.

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC
utterances.text: Sidik Ademovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were born on the 10th of February, 1969 [as interpreted], in Susnjari, municipality of Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your father is Alija, mother Hajra, nee Oric?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just to correct the transcript, it states that you were born in 1969 in the transcript, but actually you were born in 1962 in Susnjari. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, in 1962.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You're four times removed in kinship to Mr. Oric; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You've completed elementary school in Potocari in 1977?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After that, you completed the school of the Ministry for Internal Affairs of Bosnia and Herzegovina for professional police officers in Sarajevo in 1981.

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In July 1981, you were deployed at the Srebrenica police station as a police officer.

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In 1989, you enrolled at the Faculty of Political Sciences in Sarajevo, department for security?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You graduated in nineteen eighty --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not get the year.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you are a professor in security?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the area of Susnjari in Srebrenica -- we're having problems with the transcript again. You graduated in 1999; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, in 1989.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: 1999, interpreter's correction.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During the fall of Srebrenica in 1995, you and your wife lost 144 members of -- close family members.

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You personally, on the 12th of July, 1995, survived the execution in Ravni Boljum when in a few moments, in some minutes, about 500 people, your neighbours, were killed. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You are married?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you are the father of two daughters?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In 1996, you got a job at the Federal Ministry for Internal Affairs in Sarajevo, and you are still working there today, and your title is senior inspector in the operations centre of the ministry.

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Ademovic, you said that you were born in Susnjari, that you spent the war there. I would now like to ask you to look at the map which will be shown to you by the usher, and I would like you to point out some places on the map.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, it is a map that we have been using to date. It's an excerpt of the Zvornik-Kladanj map, pages 477 and 476 of the Military Institute, and it was published in 1967.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Ademovic, have you received the map?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC
utterances.text: No, not yet.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like the usher to give the witness two different coloured pens.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, yes, you can use your glasses. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the usher please give the witness two different coloured pens.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please show the Trial Chamber your village, Susnjari. Would you mark the village using one of those two pens. Could you underline the place?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC
utterances.text: I apologise, Your Honours, but I would like to use the colour green to indicate my own positions, and I would like to use the red pen in order to mark Serbian villages.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you for that remark. So will you please tell us, before the war, what was the ethnic composition of Susnjari?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC
utterances.text: The ethnic composition of Susnjari before the war was Muslim majority. About one-third of the houses were Serb houses.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Could you please show Potocari for the Trial Chamber now.

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Pale.

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Milacevici. Lehovice. Brosevici. Jaglici, and Bijecva.

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: While we're still with the map, I would like to ask you whether there was a Muslim hamlet between Susnjari and Milacevici. You cannot see it on the map, though.

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. There was a small village called Brezova Njiva. It is not indicated here, but there are some topographic symbols indicating that place.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please indicate that as BN, Brezova Njiva, at the place where you believe it is marked on the map.

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Just to clarify, these villages that you have just marked, were these Serb or Muslim villages?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC
utterances.text: These were purely Muslim villages.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please tell the Trial Chamber, how far were Susnjari and Potocari? How far apart?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC
utterances.text: From Susnjari to Potocari, as the crow flies, it's about ten kilometres, while if you take the road or go by land it's a little bit farther.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How far was Pale from Susnjari?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC
utterances.text: As the crow flies, about seven kilometres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please tell the -- or mark on this map where Srebrenica is.

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you tell us how far Susnjari is from Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC
utterances.text: My village of Susnjari, as the crow flies, is about 20 kilometres away from Srebrenica. Over land, it's further.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I will now ask you to indicate the Serb villages around the Susnjari and Jaglici and Brezova Njiva areas. Could you please start to the north. Jezestica and its hamlets. Can you show us Jezestica.

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I will begin --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Excuse me. Are you using a different colour?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I am. I'm using the colour red, and I will start to the north. To the north of Susnjari is Djermani and Jezestica. I will mark them now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you indicate Blazijevici, Jasbine, Radukici, Bukva Glava.

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And tell us is Veresinje here on the map? If not, could you show us where it is and mark it with a V.

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC
utterances.text: Veresinje has not been entered into this map but I will mark it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mark it with a V.

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you show us Kajici?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Siljkovici.

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Kravica.

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And its hamlets.

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC
utterances.text: Please excuse me, but I can do it by myself.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, but tell us the names of the villages, then.

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Mandici, Podaljevici, Opravdici, Brezik, Bukovik, Donji and Gornji Bacici, or upper and lower Bacici, Colakovici, Popovici, Ocenovici. If necessary --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's enough, thank you. Could you tell us what the villages are to the west?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC
utterances.text: West of my village of Susnjari is the general area where there are Mocila --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please answer --

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC
utterances.text: Excuse me. To west is Bratinci, Lipenovici, Zabrdje, Brezanci, Bare, Jasikovace, Manovici, Kostrice, Jeremici, Poljanci, and the general area of Ragajci, Rogac. I will mark Rogac here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Let me ask you now, when you mentioned Rogac, would you tell Their Honours whether the Rogac area is linked to another large territory inhabited by a Serb population or not.

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC
utterances.text: It is physically contiguous with Milici, which is a large village, and then by way of Vlasenica, Han Pijesak, Sokolac and the Romanija part, which has a Serb majority.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it correct that throughout the war in Han Pijesak there was a command, the main command of the army of Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please now indicate the Serb villages located to the Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. east of Susnjari, if there were any?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC
utterances.text: Ladies and gentlemen, Your Honours, on the map to the east of my village of Susnjari, there is a Serb village Dubova, which is not shown on the map.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you mark it then, please.

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I will. I'll mark it as Dubova, because I think it's very important.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Put it in, then.

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC
utterances.text: In the area where it says Kojsina, if you can see there are some dots, and I will mark this as Dubova.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you indicate Bukva Glava to Their Honours and tell them whether this is a Serb village?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mark it, please.

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The focusing is -- yes. We need to move and also we need to see what is shown on the map because the focusing is not good at all. It got worse rather than better but they have a problem and they're giving it their full attention. So it's -- I managed to mark Dubova where the witness pointed, but shall we --

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Maybe we can continue, and the witness can indicate some more villages.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you indicate the Serb villages which were to the south of the Susnjari area? For example, Sijemovo?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you indicate that? Trklat [phoen]?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC
utterances.text: I've already said that I'm circling the Serb villages in red and the Muslim villages in green.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you circled Sijemovo, please?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Where is Sijemovo? Let's see.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now we can see the map well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you indicate Sijemovo for Their Honours.

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC
utterances.text: [Indicates].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Very well.

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC
utterances.text: Is it visible?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes it is. Can you show Osredak?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC
utterances.text: [Indicates].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you indicate the general area of Orahovica?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I'll indicate Osredak and all the way south.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just Orahovica. Could you indicate that, please. Very well.

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC
utterances.text: Just a moment. Just a moment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We'll show you another map where it might be easier to find.

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC
utterances.text: Orahovica is here but this map is not sufficient.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like ask the witness to keep this map, but we will show an even broader area that the witness will speak about. So would the usher show the witness this other map as well, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: In the meantime, let's give this map a number, please. This will become Defence Exhibit D --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: D841, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: 841. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, please, have you found Orahovica on this map?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us whether Orahovica is connected to another area and what the ethnic make-up of the population there is.

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC
utterances.text: Orahovica as a local commune is linked to Pribicevac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you mark it?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC
utterances.text: I need the other map.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you found Pribicevac?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC
utterances.text: Just a moment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I may assist. Below Srebrenica. To the right.

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC
utterances.text: Pribicevci, Pribicevac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: To the right?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Can you see Skenderovici? Okay. We found it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I found it, I found it.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you indicate Brezani?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC
utterances.text: [Indicates].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Brezani. Are there any other areas inhabited by Serbs physically linked to this area?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC
utterances.text: As you can see from Orahovica via Pribicevac and Brezani, they are linked to Rajkovici and the place on the River Drina, Fakovici, which is physically separated from there by the River Drina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you indicate that, please.

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC
utterances.text: [Indicates].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in the Orahovica area can you mark a mountain area between Suceska and Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC
utterances.text: I'll take this opportunity to inform you and Their Honours that in the Orahovica area there is a place called Jogar [phoen] --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you mark it, please.

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC
utterances.text: -- which physically separates the Suceska local commune from Srebrenica. MR. DI FAZIO: If Your Honours please, I have no problem with Madam Vidovic leading the witness on all this but I think he just marked that D481 unless I'm wrong. Did I get that wrong?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No, I don't think you got that wrong. If he marked -- if you put the marking on what we are seeing on the monitor now, yes, he put it on D841. MR. DI FAZIO: I think just to be safer for the purposes of the transcript, if we are going to switch from one to the other, to enunciate it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, I think if he needs to mark this, we were using D842, Madam Vidovic, isn't it? We were using the new map.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So we give him back the new map, D842, the smaller of the two, and he marks this place -- what was the name?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Vijoger.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Where does he mark it? It has to be moved to the right. Yes, much further, please. And he's going to mark it now.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Vijoger, right.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please, before we move on, I would like to clarify something that I believe is incorrect in the transcript. I asked you first of all, when you were talking about places that were connected, we were discussing Pribicevac and Brezani, and you said they were linked to Ratkovici. Am I right?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, you are right. Pribicevac and Podranje are physically linked to Ratkovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, just please answer my question. It says here Rajkovici. You then mentioned the River Drina and Fakovici, and what did you say about Fakovici and Ratkovici?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC
utterances.text: Fakovici and Ratkovici are physically linked geographically and territorially, and they are next to the River Drina on the Bosnian side, and only the River Drina separates them off from the Republic of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. It's clear in the record now. Would you please initial both maps at the top and keep these maps with you, because we will use them during your testimony. Keep the maps, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I don't know if we have marked this second map. Not yet. This second map that was handed to the witness on which he has marked several places has been tendered and received being marked as Defence Exhibit D842, 842.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Ademovic, keep the maps. I would like to ask you some questions now. You told us that during 1990 you worked as a policeman in Srebrenica. Can you tell us exactly what you did?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I worked as an officer of the operations centre of the Srebrenica police station.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you explain to the Trial Chamber what an operations centre is in a police station?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC
utterances.text: The operations centre as a post in every police station, including the one in Srebrenica, is a post that is 20 -- has 24-hour coverage. Somebody is there 24 hours a day. That operations centre at any point continuously, 24 hours a day, receives information of any type.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just one moment. Is information received about what is going on out in the field?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC
utterances.text: Anything that happens in the field, anything.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Exactly what was your job in that post?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC
utterances.text: My task in that post was to process and gather all the information as soon as possible that I received and forward it to the authorised superior officer, if you wish.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he issue instructions for you for the work?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC
utterances.text: The superior officer would look at all the information, give his opinion on the information, he would then inform me and then I would pass the information or the instructions out to the field.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. While you were doing this job in the course of 1989 and 1990, did you know or find out anything about the activities of the Serbian state security in your area?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was that information?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC
utterances.text: We received information that officers of the DB, state security service, were working on the question of alleged Islamic fundamentalism on the territories of municipalities of Srebrenica and Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: According to the information that you had as a police officer at that time, was there any Islamic fundamentalism in that area at that time?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC
utterances.text: Our operative information about that was negative. We did not have any information about it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you understand what was actually going on in relation to the work of the Serbian state security?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what was it actually about?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC
utterances.text: It was about spreading propaganda and creating a confusing situation, a situation of intolerance in which DB officers interviewed or interrogated certain citizens, Serb citizens, in the area of Bratunac and Srebrenica and asked them or talked about this alleged Islamic fundamentalism.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please tell me whether this was happening after Milosevic came to power?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Regarding the activities of the Serbian SDB, did you have any personal contacts with people from the SDB?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was that about?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC
utterances.text: Those people talked to me on several occasions and also asked me to speak with them and asked me, amongst other things, about Islamic fundamentalism, about some Green Berets, and thirdly, and this was a key question, they asked me about the Croat defence forces, the HOS.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please explain to the Trial Chamber what HOS is?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC
utterances.text: When they first asked me, I didn't know right away, but later I learned that these were allegedly Croatian armed or intelligence services.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please tell me whether something like this did actually exist in the Srebrenica and Bratunac area?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC
utterances.text: Our operative information was negative, meaning no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the course of 1990, did you have information or not that some roads were being built which didn't exist in your area prior to that?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please tell us something about that.

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC
utterances.text: In early 1990 and then more intensely in 1991, there was speedy work to lay down new roads, particularly in Serb areas, especially in the area of Kravica where the Kravica-Siljkovici-Lipanovica-Rogac road was built. Then in the area of Podavlje [phoen], then Jadar, Pribicevac, Rad, linking it to Brezani and Ratkovici, which was then laid down directly to Fakovici, linking it to the Drina River, then roads in the area of Osata, Podravanje, Ljeskovik, Klotjevac, directly linking up with the crossing through the Bajina Basta thermoelectric power station.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did these roads pass through Muslim settlements such as Konjevic Polje, for example?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC
utterances.text: No. Here Muslim villages were deliberately bypassed, and Konjevic Polje in particular.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know who was building these roads?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, our operations -- our operative information, which was quite accessible in public, was that the contractors for these roads were Partizan Putevi from Uzice.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please tell us something about this company Partizan Putevi? Did you know anything more about this particular firm?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. The construction firm which was specialised for building roads was part of the Yugoslav People's Army but it was of a civilian nature.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have the opportunity to speak with any of the employees of that firm?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, because works were being carried out in the area of my municipality and in the area that I was responsible for as a police officer. I talked to those people because that company or that firm, the contracting firm, employed a certain number of people who actually were from my area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what did they say? Did the firm belong to the Yugoslav People's Army?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC
utterances.text: From their conversation, and this is something that we also knew, it was no secret, we knew that it did belong to the Yugoslav People's Army and a part of it to the factory in Uzice which was of a specific nature.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is Uzice a town in Serbia?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: According to what you know, were these roads of any importance during the several months before the war broke out?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, they were of major importance. That would be seen later. But specifically, the main road Polom, Zelinje, Glogova, Planina, Kravica, Siljkovici, Siljkovici - I repeat Siljkovici - Kravica, Lipenovici, Rogac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the importance of that road?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC
utterances.text: It was of military and strategic importance in order to supply the Serbian forces with weapons, personnel, and all the other logistics.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the war in Croatia have any significant effect on the events in your area in early 1991?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please tell us what happened? What did you see? What did you find out as a police officer?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC
utterances.text: When the war broke out in Croatia, it was obvious in the area of the Srebrenica municipality that many citizens of Serb ethnicity of military age went to the fronts in Croatia. And they would come back from there in uniforms and armed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what kind of an atmosphere did this create in the area of Srebrenica and Bratunac according to what you know?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC
utterances.text: According to what I came up against in the field, and according to our operational information, it had a negative effect. There was also a propaganda aspect which had a negative effect on the Muslim population, because the returnees from the front, from Croatia, told negative stories about Catholics in Croatia, mostly from the area of Vukovar, which caused a more intense degree of concern amongst the Muslim population.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could we please now play D696, which is a video. It's a Defence exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, we provided a transcript of this video recording to the interpreters.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you play it from 12.47 to 15.22.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: "[Voiceover] The most responsible people from the ministry of internal affairs from Bosnia-Herzegovina were there, and they held a press conference in Sarajevo this evening. In Kajici, the municipality of Bratunac on the regional road, unknown persons from ambush from automatic weapons fired on four persons which were in a Lada vehicle, licence plate number 280062. "On this occasion Nedzad Hodzic and Dzemo Jusic lost their, lives and Mevludin Sinanovic and Zaim Salkanovic from the village of Repovci, Bratunac municipality, were wounded. Bullet shells were found, fingerprints, and the criminal department is already working to establish the factual situation and the perpetrators. "We went to the location where a large number of Muslims gathered and they were asking for weapons, and they wanted the perpetrators to be prosecuted in a way which was not accordance with the legal system of Bosnia-Herzegovina. At the same time, the Serb population was disturbed and who to a large part had already moved to Ljubovija at this meeting Mr. Pebib and myself with the other representatives."

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Ademovic, have you seen this footage?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you recognise anyone on this footage?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I recognised Mr. Vitomir Zepinic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you recognise anyone else?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC
utterances.text: I recognised myself.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was your role in the investigation of these events?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC
utterances.text: It was my role to attend this meeting and to record the conversations and everything that was being discussed at the meeting so that later during the investigation and other activities we could use them as authentic proof of what was said at that particular meeting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was this actually a press conference?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it correct that you knew all the particulars of these events in Kajici and Kravica?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Nedzad Hodzic and Dzemo Jusic who were killed, and Mevludin Sinanovic and Zaim Salkanovic who were injured, are these Muslims?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the investigation show whether these people were armed or not?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you, for example, see the record of the on-site investigation and were you present at the on-site investigation?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I was investigating this case also. I saw several records and attended the signing of the minutes and records concerning this incident.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were these people armed?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC
utterances.text: Weapons. No, weapons were not found on the scene.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please, do you remember whether the Serb authorities or representatives from Serb authorities tried to present this event in a different light?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Through propaganda and by disseminating different misinformation, they used any opportunity to show that the guys who were killed were armed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would now like to play an audiotape, and this is Defence Exhibit 522. This is an intercept of a conversation of the 4th of September, 1991, of Radovan Karadzic and Zvonko Bajagic. This conversation has transcripts both in Bosnian and English, and the transcripts are 03232858. Could we please play the part starting from 0000 up to 0448.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] "Hello? "Good afternoon, is it you, Zvonko? "Yes, I am, Dr. Radovan. "How are you? "Well, I'm fine. "What have you been doing? "Should I start from the beginning? "Okay, could you talk harder, please? "To start from the beginning. "Okay. "I don't know if you have been on top of things since Friday? "I know that they shot at the president of the Executive Council, that fellow was arrested and then released. "Yes. "Then Muslims were headed to Kravica village. Was their intention to attack or what? "No. "Well, well, down there after Friday ... "Yes? "Down there, related to these things, there were some fighting. "Yes, yes. "After Friday the SUP deployed the police force in these villages. The hot spots. So only the Serbs were deployed in Kravica. "Yes. "Because that is what they demanded and the patrols, consisting both of Serbs and Muslims were in Konjevic Polje and that other place over there Loljici. "Uh-huh, good. "That has been an around-the-clock duty. There has been this duty and the village guard ever since. After those two persons from Han Pijesak were wounded at the barricade. "After that? "After that and before the shooting before the president of the Executive Council. "Okay. "Two persons were wounded, and the motive for it was putting up the barricade up there in Han Pijesak. They informed you about that. "Yes. Two men were wounded, very well. "And then after the wounding there was the attempt, the assassination attempt at the president of the Executive Council down there. "Okay. Then again Serbs were wounded, so again they shot at a Serb. "No, listen, to keep you abreast of things, well, let's leave the president of the Executive Council aside. Do you know there was an attempt to kill him but they did not kill him? "And did they injure him? "No, they did not. "But this president is a Serb, isn't he? "Yes, the president of the Executive Council of the Bratunac Municipal Assembly. "Okay. But these two men in Han Pijesak were also Serbs? "And these two who were wounded in Han Pijesak were Serbs. "Okay. "Listen, last night these four men in that car who road slowly through Kravica, their main military strategic on behalf of the SVA and the biggest stool-pigeon was in that car with three other men. "Yes, yes. "And they drove two times through Kravica. "And Kravica is a Serbian village? Kravica is a Serbian village like the Mokro region. "Yes, yes, yes. "It is part of the Glasinac area. "Yes, yes. "And they were riding through twice. They drove to Konjevic Polje. Konjevic Polje is a Muslim village. "Yes, yes. So it seems that they were provoking, weren't they? "Yes, they were riding through with all four windows rolled down and barrels of their machine-guns sticking out of the windows. "Mm-hmm. "And a police patrol gave them twice the sign to stop. "Uh-huh. "At two spots the police gave them the signs to stop but they refused to do it. "Uh-huh. "That is the one patrolling through Kravica. "Okay. "And the local villagers walk along with these patrols. "Okay. "Up there by the exit from Kravica in the direction of Bratunac there is a borderline between Serbs and Muslims there and Serbs keep watch there. They have their sentries there. "Yes, yes. "And they received the message. Well, some of these were provoking with machine-guns. The police tried to stop them at two points. They did want to stop, so these men were tied -- up there tried to stopped them. They refused. They opened fire. They killed two and wounded one of them. "Whom did they kill? "They killed two Muslims. Not the main one. "Uh-huh. "Well, that one is lucky but they killed two of them. "Okay. "Furthermore, earlier today now the Muslim people went down to Bratunac and they are rejoicing to go to attack Kravica. "Uh-huh. "Just let me see. A vehicle has arrived. Is he coming here? Okay, okay, it is our man. But in the meantime, the MUP forces arrived in Bratunac. "Okay. "And not long ago a helicopter with MUP personnel flew across the way to Bratunac. "Okay. "We saw through the binoculars that there were more personnel. "Okay. "Furthermore, the Kravica men are still holding their positions. They do not allow anyone to -- they shoot if a single man from MUP should put their foot on their territory. "Okay. "It can easily happen that those from up there move in an organised manner before the dark and that will cause then a frontal ... "To move in an organised manner? "Yes. If the MUP and one of them from down there moved towards Kravica. "Yes. "They will come under fire, under machine-gun fire. "Okay. "That's it. The Kravica men, they decided that firmly and they will not give it up. "Are they armed? "Yes, they are. Furthermore, their people, Serbs from the villages having a common border with villages with Muslim population are evacuated. They are moving across the Drina, and they go to the centre of the village and into the woods. "Okay. "Everything is deserted. It is horrible to see that. They would come to Milici to ask for help. "Okay. "Maybe some of these volunteers should go. They also asked me to go to Han Pijesak. Thus, I have come home from Milici and I am reporting to you. As far as I can see, nobody contacted you about these things. "No, nobody contacted me about this. "Well, in general, you should know that this is extremely urgent. I think that someone should show up immediately, otherwise it will be trouble. "Who needs to show up? "At the ones who can be the most influential ones. You and someone on behalf of the SDA, someone who can ... "And what should they do?"

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Ademovic, you heard that. Can you tell Their Honours who Radovan Karadzic was at the time?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC
utterances.text: First of all, I recognised the voice of Mr. Radovan Karadzic. Radovan Karadzic was the president of the SDS of Bosnia and Herzegovina, a member of the Presidency, and a public figure in politics who at that time spoke often and spoke a lot.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please, have you heard of Zvonko Bajagic?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Zvonko Bajagic was a local politician, a member of the SDS in Vlasenica, in Vlasenica municipality.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Ademovic, you heard this conversation. Is Karadzic discussing with Bajagic the event in Kravica referred to by Mr. Veto Zepanic a little while ago, those murders?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, precisely so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is Mr. Vito Zepanic a Serb?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you notice that Bajagic says that four Muslims were driving up and down Kravica in a car with weapons? What actually happened?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. He says that they drove up and down and that they had weapons. On the contrary. They were not walking around -- driving up and down. They were not armed. They were going from Konjevic Polje towards Hranca where they originated from.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Did you notice that Mr. Bajagic says the people of Kravica are holding their position? They're not allowing anyone to enter. Not a single member of the MUP can enter. If he crosses over to their territory, they shoot. At the time of these events did you have any specific knowledge of this?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. One of the leaders of the Bratunac police station, Senad Hodzic, tried to enter with a police patrol into Kravica, and he did not succeed. He ran into an ambush before entering Kravica. They were shot at, and they withdrew. They never entered Kravica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you agree that the events referred to here took place in September 1992 [as interpreted]?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, September 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you notice that Karadzic asked --

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, it says 1992 in the record.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] September 1991.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you notice that Karadzic asks Bajagic whether the people of Kravica are armed and that Bajagic replies, "Yes, they are"?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I noticed that well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please, you said that you received various kinds of operative information. Did you have any operative information connected with Kravica and its hamlets with respect to the fact commented upon here, that is, that the men of Kravica were armed in September 1991? What was your operative information? Can you tell Their Honours?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC
utterances.text: Our operative information showed that the area of Kravica was armed when certain -- a certain number of units withdrew from the war theatre in Croatia where parts of the convoy late at night were stopped, and they remained in the area of Kravica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have any information as to where these weapons were stored, if they were stored?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. We also had such operative information. The weapons were stored in certain areas in the general area of Kravica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have any knowledge about the existence of depots and, if so, where were they?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. One of the depots was in Kajici, in the direction of Jezestica. Another of the depots was in the area of Brezik. A third depot was in the very centre of Kravica, the Zadruci Magazin [phoen], and certain rooms in the primary school. The fourth of these depots was a cave overlooking the church in Kravica in the direction of Popovici and Mandici. It was to the north of Kravica, to the north of the church, and this cave was a large one, a very roomy one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where did you personally get this information, from whom?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC
utterances.text: We got this information both from Muslims, but its authenticity was confirmed by Serbs who at that time were still of a communist or socialist orientation, in favour of the former regime.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: While listening to this conversation, did you observe that Radovan Karadzic says, "Get along wisely, as best you can. Don't allow anyone to enter Serb villages but these volunteers who are coming." Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I noticed that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After this event in September 1991, did a single Muslim dare spend time in a Serb village, Jezestica, Lipenovici, Rogac, Brezani where you lived?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC
utterances.text: No. Quite the contrary. Bus stops in Kravica were no longer used by Muslims. All the local approaches through Jezestica, Kajici, and the general area of Kravica, the local roads were closed to the Muslims. They could only use them for transit from Bratunac towards Konjevic Polje.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The regular police forces of Bosnia and Herzegovina, could they, after September 1991, do their job in Kravica, for example?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC
utterances.text: As of September 1991, the regular police force no longer had any control or any information as to what was actually happening there. Access was open only to Serb policemen and members of the narrow circle of SDS leaders.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In connection with these events in Kravica, concerning the murders, did you discuss these with your Serb colleagues?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC
utterances.text: Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment. Let's go into private session for a moment, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Before the break, I have two more questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Go ahead. Let's finish with these two questions.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please, Witness, you told us that Kravica and its hamlets was armed. While performing your duties, did you observe any other activities by the Serb population in November and December 1991 after these murders?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you see?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC
utterances.text: In the area of Jezestica and Djermani, which are part of Kravica, there began to appear guards where people were armed, and they started digging trenches and dugouts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And were these people Serbs?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Will you now tell us exactly where they were digging these dugouts and trenches?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC
utterances.text: In front of Jezestica on the line running from Djermani, Veresinje, Siljkovici, Hajducko Groblje, the Hajduk cemetery, to the west, Lipenovici, Mratinci, Poljanci, Radukici, Kajici. That's the area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, now is a convenient time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So we'll have a 30-minute break starting from now. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, I noticed that I was proceeding quite slowly so I would like you to make your answers as brief as possible. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could the usher now show the witness exhibit -- actually, it's a copy of a hunting permit of the Javor Srebrenica Hunting Society. Is it correct that you personally gave me this document, Witness?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's a paper which is actually a hunting permit?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you a hunter before the war?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have hunting equipment?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. A hunting rifle and binoculars as well as some other equipment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As a hunter, did you move around in this area during the war?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Earlier you spoke about lines which you said were drug in different locations in Jezestica. Did you personally have the opportunity to see those lines with your own eyes?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Very often in that area, because that area is connected physically to my village, I would frequently meet Mr. Dragan Ilic, and we spent some time hunting in that area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could this exhibit or this document be given an exhibit number, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. This document, Ms. Vidovic, will become Defence Exhibit D843 and that consists of two pages, one being the photocopy of the original document referred to by the witness and the second page is the English translation thereof. Yes. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: While you were performing your duties and as you moved around in that area, as a hunter did you have information about the arming of some other areas in the Podrinje region if there were such areas?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. As a hunter as well as a police station officer I was out in the field a lot and we had operative information that Serbs were arming themselves in Podravanje, Ratkovici, Fakovici, Brezani, Orahovica, Osredak, Sijemovo, Studenac, and Sase, Bjelovac, wherever there were Serbs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember any specific events from that time?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us if you remember anything in relation to Dubova which you indicated earlier on the map and said it was important?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. In Dubova we confiscated three automatic rifles from the Ilic family. Excuse me. Excuse me. Not Ilic but Lukic. The Lukic family. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From March 1992 onwards, was it a rare occurrence to receive informs about the arming in that area or did this happen frequently? About the arming of the Serb population.

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC
utterances.text: We at the police station received more and more information from hour to hour indicating that Serbs were arming themselves in all parts of the Srebrenica and Bratunac municipalities.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have information about who was arming the local Serbs?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC
utterances.text: Our operative information indicated that this was done by representatives of the SDS and their associates in neighbouring villages.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have information about the role of the JNA in this arming, if there was a role of the JNA?
